q: 1. Sensitiveness of a level tube is designated by
options: length of bubble of level tube
explain: The sensitivity of a bubble/level tube is directly related to the radius of curvature of its inner surface; a larger radius gives a more sensitive tube.

q: 2. Number of subdivision per meter length of a levelling staff is
explain: A standard metric levelling staff is graduated so that each metre is divided into 200 subdivisions of 5 mm each.

q: 3. Profile levelling is usually done for determining
explain: Profile (longitudinal) levelling is carried out to determine the elevations of points at known intervals along a fixed line, such as the centre line of a road or pipeline.

q: 4. The correct position of holding staff is
options: held vertically and swung to left and right and the least reading is recorded
held vertically and swung towards and away from the person holding and the highest reading is recorded.
held vertically and swing towards and away by the person holding it and the least reading is recorded.
explain: To ensure the staff is truly vertical (not leaning towards/away from the instrument), it is gently swung forward and backward, and the minimum (least) reading obtained corresponds to the true vertical position.

q: 5. For high sensitivity of the bubble tube
options: a liquid of low viscosity is used
a liquid of low surface tension is used
the bubble space should be long
explain: A longer bubble space in the level tube increases sensitivity, since the bubble then travels a greater length for a given tilt, making small tilts more noticeable.

q: 6. Determining the difference in elevation between two points on the surface of the earth, is known as
explain: Leveling, in its most general definition, is the branch of surveying concerned with determining the difference in elevation between points on the earth's surface.

q: 7. During levelling generally instrumental error is occuring due to
explain: Collimation error occurs when the line of sight is not truly horizontal even when the bubble is centered, which is a classic instrumental error.

q: 8. The sensitivity of the bubble tube can be increased by
options: decreasing the radius of curvature of tube
increasing the diameter of the tube
explain: Sensitivity increases with an increase in the radius of curvature, the length of the bubble, and the internal diameter of the tube.

q: 9. If temperature increases the sensitivity of a bubble tube
explain: Increased temperature causes the liquid to expand, which decreases the length of the bubble and consequently its sensitivity.

q: 10. In case of leveling staff readings are taken by (In case of target staff)
explain: In target leveling, the instrument man signals the staff man to move the target; once aligned, the staff man reads the value from the staff.

q: 11. Instrumental error in levelling is error due to
explain: All mentioned factors—lack of adjustment, poor bubble response, and loose mechanical parts—are categorized as instrumental errors.

q: 12. Permanent adjustment are carried out to
options: establish a fixed relationship between its fundamental axes
explain: Permanent adjustments ensure that the line of collimation, bubble axis, and vertical axis remain in their correct relative geometric positions.

q: 13. The method of levelling used to carry out the reconnaissance of area is
explain: Fly leveling is a rapid method of leveling used to establish approximate elevations or to connect a benchmark to a starting point during reconnaissance.

q: 14. The method of levelling in which the heights of mountains are found by observing the temperature at which water boils is known as
explain: Hypsometry is the method of determining elevation by observing the boiling point of water, which varies with atmospheric pressure (and hence altitude).

q: 15. The method of surveying used for determining the relative height of points on the surface of the earth is called
explain: Differential levelling is the method specifically used to determine the relative heights (difference in elevation) of points on the earth's surface.

q: 16. A line normal to the plumb line at all points is known as
explain: A level line, being everywhere perpendicular to the plumb line (direction of gravity), is a curved line following the level surface of the earth.

q: 17. The sensitivity of the bubble tube expressed in terms of angular value of one division of the bubble is given by
explain: Sensitivity $\alpha = s / (nD)$, where $s$ is the total staff intercept and $D$ is the distance; for one division, it is expressed as $s/D$ radians.

q: 18. The last reading of levelling is always a
explain: A leveling circuit or run always concludes with a Fore Sight (FS) on a point of known or final elevation.

q: 19. To find the true difference of level between two points, the level should be kept
options: at either of the two points
exactly midway between the two points
at any point on the line joining the two points
explain: To eliminate the effects of curvature, refraction, and collimation error most effectively, the level should ideally be set up exactly midway between the two points being observed.

q: 20. The first reading of leveling is always
explain: Every leveling operation must start with a Back Sight (BS) taken on a point of known elevation (Bench Mark) to establish the Height of Instrument.

q: 21. If the BM of a station A is 500 m. The back sight reading at the point A is 2 m and fore sight reading of station B is 3 m, then find the RL of station B
explain: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL + BS = 500 + 2 = 502 m. RL of B = HI - FS = 502 - 3 = 499 m.

q: 22. In levelling, the correction for curvature (in meters) is equal to
explain: The standard formula for the curvature correction, with D in kilometres, is Cc = 0.0785*D2 metres.

q: 23. In levelling, the correction for combined curvature and refraction (in meters) is equal to
explain: Accounting for the effect of atmospheric refraction (about 1/7th of the curvature effect, in the opposite sense), the combined correction reduces to 0.0673*D2 metres, with D in kilometres.

q: 24. The following sights are taken on the turning point
explain: At a turning (change) point, both a fore sight (to close the previous instrument setup) and a back sight (to begin the next instrument setup) are taken.

q: 25. In a constant level tube, size of the bubble remains constant because upper wall is
explain: In a constant-bubble level tube, the upper wall has a relatively larger radius of curvature compared to the main curved surface, which keeps the bubble length constant despite temperature changes.

q: 26. If the level tube is out of adjustment by an angle e, when the telescope is rotated through 180°, it becomes
explain: Rotating the telescope by 180° doubles the angular error relative to the vertical axis, hence 2e.

q: 27. "Cross-sectioning" and "Longitudinal sectioning" is
options: when less number of intermediate sight exist
explain: Profile leveling involves taking readings along a center line (longitudinal) and at right angles to it (cross-sectioning) to map the terrain.

q: 28. The points A and B are 1530 m apart across a wide river... The true difference in level between A and B would be
explain: Using the reciprocal leveling formula: True Difference = [(B1 - A1) + (B2 - A2)] / 2. Based on the table: [(3.810 - 2.165) + (2.355 - 0.91)] / 2 = [1.645 + 1.445] / 2 = 1.545 m.

q: 29. During levelling staff readings are taken 1.0, 0.8 & 0.6 from consecutive horizontal cross hairs, the staff intercept should be
explain: The staff intercept is the difference between the top and bottom hair readings: 1.0 - 0.6 = 0.4.

q: 30. Parallax is an adjustment carried out in
explain: Removal of parallax (by properly focusing the eyepiece and objective) is a key temporary adjustment carried out in levelling instruments before taking readings.

q: 31. In survey it was recorded that Sum of Rise = 0, then
options: the survey had many invert readings
explain: If the sum of all rises recorded is zero (meaning no rises were recorded at all, only falls), it indicates the ground is continuously falling throughout the leveling run.

q: 32. The function of levelling head is
options: to attach the theodolite to the tripod
to provide a bearing for the outer hollow spindle
to provide a mean of levelling the instrument
explain: The leveling head serves as the interface between the tripod and the instrument, supporting the vertical axis and housing the leveling mechanism.

q: 33. The method of finding out the difference in elevation between two points for eliminating the effect of curvature and refraction is
explain: Per the answer key provided in this text, differential levelling is identified as the method used here, since it is the general procedure for determining elevation differences over multiple set-ups, effectively managing curvature and refraction through careful instrument placement.

q: 34. The very first reading taken is called
explain: The very first staff reading taken at the start of a leveling operation (on a point of known elevation) is always a back sight.

q: 35. Which of the following can be neutralized by setting the level midway between the two stations?
options: Error due to both curvature and refraction
explain: By setting up the level exactly midway between two stations, the combined effects of both earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction are equal and opposite at both sights, and hence get neutralized.

q: 36. For removing the parallax
options: the eye-piece should be focused for distinct vision of cross-hairs
the image of the object should be brought in the plane of cross-hairs
explain: Removing parallax completely requires both actions together - focusing the eyepiece for clear cross-hairs and focusing the objective to bring the image into the plane of the cross-hairs.

q: 37. Ten readings were recorded in a level field book. If the instrument was shifted after 2nd & 6th readings, then the fore sights are
explain: Fore sights are the last readings taken before each instrument shift, plus the final closing reading; since the instrument was shifted after the 2nd and 6th readings, and the leveling run ends at the 10th reading, the fore sights are the 2nd, 6th, and 10th readings.

q: 38. Correction for refraction for a distance of 1 km =
explain: Refraction correction is taken as about one-seventh of the curvature correction: 0.0785/7 approximately equal to 0.0112 m for a distance of 1 km.

q: 39. A plumb line is
options: a line parallel to a vertical line
a line perpendicular to level line
a line perpendicular to the horizontal line
explain: A plumb line is, by definition, a vertical line, indicating the direction of gravity at a point.

q: 40. Permanent adjustments of a level are
explain: A dumpy/tilting level typically requires three permanent adjustments - of the bubble tube, of the line of collimation, and of the cross hair - to bring it into correct working order.

q: 41. Number of subdivisions per metre length of a leveling staff is
explain: A standard leveling staff graduated in metres is typically subdivided into 500 parts per metre (giving graduations of 2 mm each).
